newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain asks France to extradite suspected ETA head.
newsitem.headline: Spain asks France to extradite suspected ETA head.

text.p: Spain on Monday asked France to extradite Jose Luis Urrusolo, believed by Spanish officials to be a leader of the Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA, who was arrested in Bordeaux last week.
The High Court said it had applied for his extradition on charges that he was party to an attack in Barcelona in 1991 that killed two police officers.
Spanish officials have said they suspect Urrusolo, who they believe to be one of the ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) movement's top three members, of involvement in as many as 16 killings.
French police arrested Urrusolo, armed with a handgun and carrying false papers, in Bordeaux last Thursday. He is in custody in Paris.
France handed over another suspected ETA member on Monday.

Eulalia Aramendi, who had completed a four-year prison sentence in France, is wanted in Spain on suspicion of killing a postman in 1984 and being involved in an attack on a Civil Guard barracks in 1985.
Cooperation between France and Spain has led to more than 200 arrests in the past decade. ETA has killed around 800 people since 1968 in its campaign for an independent Basque state.
